family.preferred_name: RecA/Rad51-type recombinases of bacteria and plant organelles
family.summary: The bacterial RecA recombinases and the organellar RecA homologs that plants inherited from the plastid and mitochondrial endosymbionts. A member nucleates on single-stranded DNA, polymerizes into a right-handed helical nucleoprotein filament, searches duplex DNA for homology and catalyses strand exchange, coupling the reaction to ATP binding and hydrolysis through its P-loop. In bacteria the activated filament has a second role: it is the platform that stimulates autocatalytic cleavage of the LexA-family repressor and so induces the damage response. Of the 673 reviewed members, 670 are bacterial RecA proteins in SF1; the remaining three are Arabidopsis organellar homologs. The subfamily names are a PANTHER naming artifact and do not mean the bacterial members are mitochondrial.
family.coherence_reason: ssDNA binding, filament formation and ATP-dependent strand exchange hold across the family, including the organellar homologs, which perform recombination on organelle genomes. Only the LexA-cleavage role is lineage-dependent, since it requires a LexA-family repressor to act on.

subfamilies.label: MITOCHONDRIAL DNA REPAIR PROTEIN RECA HOMOLOG-RELATED
subfamilies.description: The bacterial RecA proteins: 670 of the family's 673 reviewed members, spanning the whole domain. Despite the subfamily name, which PANTHER took from the plant nomenclature of its relatives, these are the cytoplasmic bacterial recombinases and SOS inducers. Some alleles carry mobile intervening sequences: M. tuberculosis RecA is translated as a precursor containing the PI-MtuI intein, which excises itself by protein splicing and, assayed as the excised sequence, is an ATP-dependent site-specific endonuclease in its own right.

node_assessments.assessment_reason: The PANTHER 19 treeinfo service reports PTN000534381 as the ROOT node of PTHR45900, a speciation node with taxonomic range LUCA, so the assertion reaches every member including the plant organellar homologs. That is the right depth: nucleation on single-stranded DNA is the step that defines the whole family's mechanism, it is assayed in both seeds, and the organellar homologs perform the same recombination chemistry on organelle genomes. Note that both E. coli RecA and M. tuberculosis RecA appear in their own WITH/FROM for this term, which is the expected marker that experimental grounding exists on those targets, not circularity.

node_assessments.assessment_reason: The seed is E. coli RecA, which really is a component of the Pol V mutasome: the active complex is UmuD'2C-RecA-ATP. But the term names a specific complex built from the umuDC gene products, and it has been placed at the family root (LUCA), so every RecA homolog inherits membership of an enterobacterial translesion-synthesis complex. The over-reach is checkable in GOA: Arabidopsis RECA2 (Q8RY99) and RECA3 (Q9ZUP2), both mitochondrially targeted plant proteins, carry GO:0009355 IBA from this node and this seed, and so does M. tuberculosis RecA (P9WHJ3), whose genome has no umuDC at all. Mycobacteria instead use the ImuA'-ImuB-DnaE2 cassette, described in the literature as the non-orthologous replacement of the umuDC system, so the inherited complex does not exist in that lineage. The term belongs on the enterobacterial RecA clade at most, and arguably only on members shown to participate in a Pol V complex.

node_assessments.assessment_reason: The activity belongs to a mobile element, not to the recombinase. The seed P9WHJ3 is translated as a precursor that contains the PI-MtuI intein, which excises itself by protein splicing; UniProt lists it as a separate chain with its own name and EC number and states plainly that PI-MtuI is an endonuclease. The seed's own experimental endonuclease annotation (PMID:11850426) is therefore an activity of the intein, and placing it at the family root propagates a homing endonuclease to every RecA protein in the tree. Again checkable in GOA: Arabidopsis RECA2 and RECA3 both carry GO:0004520 IBA from this node and this seed. No node in a RecA tree is the right place for this term, because inteins are not inherited with the recombinase: the annotation should sit on the PI-MtuI chain, not on RecA.

family.notes: Written while promoting modules/bacterial_imuabc_damage_induced_mutagenesis.yaml to COMPLETE, whose optional RecA signalling step is grounded here through P. putida RecA. Three of the five root-placed PAINT assertions are sound (ssDNA binding, strand exchange, recombinational repair); two over-reach, and both are reported for upstream attention. GO:0009355 (DNA polymerase V complex) propagates an enterobacterial complex to plant organellar homologs and to mycobacterial RecA, whose lineage replaced umuDC with the very cassette this module describes. GO:0004520 (DNA endonuclease activity) propagates the activity of the PI-MtuI intein carried by the M. tuberculosis recA allele, which was assayed on the excised intervening sequence (PMID:11850426) rather than on RecA; the intein evidence is cited from that cached publication rather than from the UniProt flat file, since there is no local genes/MYCTU/recA folder against which a flat-file quote could be checked. Neither affects the module's own exemplar: Q88ME4 carries no IBA rows at all. Node depth was read from the PANTHER 19 treeinfo service (pantherdb.org/services/oai/pantherdb/treeinfo?family=PTHR45900), which reports PTN000534381 as the ROOT node with taxonomic range LUCA. The subfamily labels are PANTHER's official names, verbatim, and are misleading for SF1: those 670 members are bacterial RecA proteins, not mitochondrial.
